axis_supply.supply_status: CHRONICALLY INADEQUATE - Italian logistics struggled throughout North Africa campaign. British Mediterranean interdiction (Malta-based RAF/RN) sank 15-22% of Axis convoys Q1 1942. Even supplies reaching Tripoli faced 1,400 km journey to Gazala line (or 800 km from Benghazi). Italian trucks consumed 30-40% of fuel cargo making delivery runs. German units received priority allocation - DAK operated at 85-95% supply while Ariete at 60-70%. Fuel reserves typically 4-6 days (versus 7-10 days for German units). Ammunition rationed - Italian artillery fired fraction of British volumes. Spare parts catastrophically short, especially tank transmissions and engines. Tank operational readiness only 60-65% (vs 80-85% for German panzer divisions). Captured British supplies at Benghazi (29 Jan 1942) provided temporary relief but convoy losses resumed.

allied_supply.supply_status: Improved from Q4 1941. Division established in defensive positions along northern sector of Gazala Line with static supply depots. Primary supply route from Tobruk (35km) and Benghazi (250km). Water supply adequate from coastal wells and desalination. Division was 5,570 men under-strength as of 8 January 1942 (17,617 vs authorized 23,187). Supply situation stable during defensive preparations but constrained by limited port capacity at Tobruk and long haul from Egypt.
